correctness.rationale: By symmetry take p>=q, so the hypothesis gives p>=2. The two-point transform H(a,b)=(a+b,a-b) has exact norms 1 from ell_1^2 to ell_infinity^2 and sqrt(2) from ell_2^2 to itself. Riesz--Thorin with theta=2/p gives ||H|| from ell_{p'}^2 to ell_p^2 at most 2^(1/p); the exact two-dimensional norm comparison to ell_q multiplies by 2^(1/q-1/p), and a coordinate vector attains the resulting bound 2^(1/q). Hence A=2^(-1/q)H has norm one. Composing A with the coordinate reflection gives another norm-one B; coordinate vectors and the triangle inequality show ||A+B||=||A-B||=2. The VNJ quotient is therefore 2, matching the universal upper bound. The coordinate two-dimensional subspaces are isometric for the injective norm, so the witness extends to all m,n>=2. The proof includes p=2 and p=infinity endpoints and requires no numerical extrapolation.
